before: Would regulate large electric load customers of at least 50 MW, require co-located electric supplier licensing, require new large-load tariffs, require 100 percent load coverage plus reserve margin from new generation subject to waivers, and require financial guarantees to protect other ratepayers.
after: Would regulate customers with peak demand of at least 50 MW and license co-located suppliers. A co-located supplier would cover anticipated load plus reserve from generation entering service on or after July 1, 2026, or an adequate incremental increase to existing nameplate capacity, subject to a ratepayer and planning-based waiver. Proposed tariffs for later-interconnecting customers would separately require new generation that had not cleared a capacity auction, with a demand-flexibility waiver for customers not served by co-located suppliers, and financial protections for other ratepayers.
